plain_description.what: Real tree builds on two intent datasets with known label hierarchies (MASSIVE and CLINC150). The trees are compared with flat k-means at the same number of groups and with a supervised upper bound. Checks cover partition quality, hierarchy, address stability, filing new items, and abstaining on borderline items.
plain_description.why: On data where the true answer is known, it tests whether the label-free tree recovers real structure as well as standard clustering does.
plain_description.information: Result (builds, no judge calls): the label-free tree partitions as well as k-means (judged equivalent on both datasets). It keeps its cell addresses as well as k-means when slot words in a query are swapped (for example a different city name). It files new items better by nearest leaf than by walking down the tree. Its hierarchy beats a simple average-link grouping of the same leaves (interval only). It fails against label-conditioned per-class prototypes, which is a registered failure. This is one draw and one embedder, and 'equivalent' does not mean 'better'.
